name: Chip Fabrication
blurb: Who actually manufactures AI silicon, on what process, and where.

items.name: GlobalFoundries
items.note: Trailing-edge and specialty nodes; the US-based volume foundry for everything that does not need leading edge

items.name: Intel Foundry
items.note: Intel's external foundry business; 18A is its leading-edge node bid for AI silicon

items.name: Samsung Foundry
items.note: The second leading-edge logic foundry; gate-all-around SF3/SF2 nodes

items.name: SMIC
items.note: China's leading foundry and the fabrication path for domestic AI accelerators under export controls

items.name: TSMC
items.note: Fabricates nearly every leading AI accelerator - NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, Google TPU - on N5/N4/N3 nodes; corporate site bot-walls verification, so the source is its SEC 20-F filing index

reading.body:
TSMC fabricates nearly every leading AI accelerator on advanced nodes, while Samsung operates as the only other leading-edge logic foundry, creating a two-source dependency for cutting-edge AI silicon that directly constrains global AI compute capacity.

The five major chip fabs divide along two tiers. TSMC and Samsung compete on leading-edge process nodes used in AI accelerators. Intel Foundry aims to enter this tier with its 18A node. Below them, GlobalFoundries serves the trailing-edge and specialty market. SMIC operates outside this hierarchy due to export controls, serving as China's domestic fabrication path for AI accelerators.

This structure creates a hard constraint on AI scaling. TSMC's dominance means that any AI company seeking state-of-the-art compute must compete for capacity at a single facility. Samsung provides redundancy but limited relief. New fabs take years to reach volume production and billions in capital. The data shows who can make AI chips, but not how much capacity exists, how full they are, or what lead times look like. A reader concerned with AI scaling limits should track TSMC's utilization rates and the timeline for Intel Foundry and Samsung to absorb AI demand they cannot currently handle.

The geographic and political dimension matters for power and buildings. TSMC operates in Taiwan. Samsung in South Korea. Intel Foundry is building US capacity. This geographic split means AI scaling depends on multiple countries' power grids, manufacturing infrastructure, and export policies, not just the physics of silicon.
